title: Nonpositivity of the kernel beyond a threshold
statement: Fix natural numbers $t$ and $n$ with $t + 1 \le n$, and let $a$ be a real number lying strictly to the left of every real zero of the Krawtchouk polynomial $K_t^{(n)}$; that is, $a < \xi$ whenever $K_t^{(n)}(\xi) = 0$. Then there is a real threshold $\eta$ such that the truncated Christoffel--Darboux kernel satisfies $\Phi_{n,t}(a, x) \le 0$ for every integer $x$ with $\eta \le x \le n$.
hypotheses_covered: a lies strictly below every real zero of K_t^{(n)}
x is an integer (natural number) with x ≤ n
x is at least the threshold η
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses ($t + 1 \le n$ and $a$ strictly below every real zero of
$K_t^{(n)}$), there exists a threshold $\eta$ such that $\Phi_{n,t}(a,x) \le 0$ for
every integer $x$ with $\eta \le x \le n$.
